```{r}
#| label: blinks-by-bin
#| fig-height: 5
#| results: asis
# Blinks by condition (dataQualityMetrics' blinkRows): one row per subject x
# bin, from the vertical EOG of the trials that were averaged.
if (nrow(blk) == 0) {
  cat(paste0("\n\nNo subject has a vertical EOG this report recognises (a channel named VEOG ",
             "or VEOG-bipolar, or VEOG-lower, IO1 or IO2 with FP2 or FP1 above it), so blinks ",
             "could not be compared between conditions.\n\n"))
} else {
  sources <- blk %>% distinct(dataset, source) %>% count(source, name = "n")
  cat(sprintf("\n\nThe vertical EOG was %s.\n\n",
              paste(sprintf("%s (%d subject%s)", sources$source, sources$n,
                            ifelse(sources$n == 1, "", "s")), collapse = "; ")))
  if (n_distinct(blk$bin) < 2) {
    cat("Only one bin is present, so there is no between-condition comparison to make here.\n\n")
  } else {
    bp <- ggplot(blk, aes(x = bin, y = pct_blinks, group = dataset)) +
      geom_line(colour = "grey65", alpha = 0.7) +
      geom_point(colour = alz_blue, size = 1.6) +
      stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line",
                   colour = alz_red, linewidth = 1.2) +
      stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "point",
                   colour = alz_red, size = 3) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Averaged trials with a blink (%)",
           subtitle = "Grey: individual subjects. Red: mean across subjects") +
      alz_theme()
    print(bp)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: blinks-by-bin-test
#| results: asis
# Friedman, as for the rejection rate above and for the same reasons: blink
# percentages are bounded, skewed and often 0. Subjects without every bin
# are left out, and counted.
if (nrow(blk) > 0 && n_distinct(blk$bin) >= 2 && n_distinct(blk$dataset) >= 2) {
  wide <- blk %>% select(dataset, bin, pct_blinks) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = bin, values_from = pct_blinks)
  complete_rows <- wide %>% drop_na()
  n_dropped <- nrow(wide) - nrow(complete_rows)
  if (nrow(complete_rows) >= 2) {
    mat <- as.matrix(complete_rows %>% select(-dataset))
    if (all(apply(mat, 1, function(r) length(unique(r))) == 1)) {
      cat("\n\nEvery subject blinked in the same share of trials in every bin, so there is nothing to test.\n\n")
    } else {
      ft <- friedman.test(mat)
      cat(sprintf(paste0("\nA Friedman test across %d subject(s) with a complete set of bins ",
                         "found %s evidence that the share of trials with a blink differs ",
                         "between conditions, χ²(%d) = %s, *p* %s.\n\n"),
                  nrow(complete_rows),
                  ifelse(ft$p.value < .05, "**significant**", "no significant"),
                  ft$parameter, apa_num(ft$statistic), apa_p(ft$p.value)))
      if (ft$p.value < .05) {
        cat(paste0("Blinks are then a potential confound: whatever of them the correction ",
                   "left in the scalp channels differs between the conditions it is compared ",
                   "across. Rejecting the trials with a blink near the stimulus, or checking ",
                   "the effect at channels far from the eyes, are the usual safeguards.\n\n"))
      }
    }
  }
  if (n_dropped > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("*%d subject(s) were left out of that test for having no assessable trials in at least one bin.*\n\n", n_dropped))
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: veog-by-bin
#| fig-height: 4.5
# Equal blink rates can still differ in timing, which an averaged waveform
# shows and a count does not.
if (nrow(veog) > 0 && n_distinct(veog$bin) >= 2) {
  ga <- veog %>% group_by(bin, time_ms) %>%
    summarise(veog_uv = mean(veog_uv, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  vp <- ggplot(ga, aes(x = time_ms, y = veog_uv, colour = bin)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(x = "Time (ms)", y = "Vertical EOG (µV)", colour = NULL,
         subtitle = "Each bin's average, meaned across subjects") +
    alz_theme()
  print(vp)
}
```
